overview: Qualitative study in one internal medicine residency from October 2026 to March 2027: semi-structured interviews with residents and faculty assessors, and focus groups with chief residents and programme administrators, analysed with reflexive thematic analysis; findings reported to the competency committee in May 2027.
population: Residents in training years 1 to 3 (purposive sample across years, gender, international and local graduates, and low and high assessment counts), faculty assessors across inpatient and clinic rotations, the three chief residents, and the four programme administrators. Residents with pending remediation decisions are not approached during those months.
exposure: The EPA assessment system as experienced: the target of 12 app-based assessments per rotation, entrustment ratings and narrative comments.
procedures: The research assistant, who has no role in progression decisions, sends invitations through the residents' association and the department office. Interviews (45 to 60 minutes, in person or by video, in lunch hours) follow a guide covering the last rotation, how assessments were requested and completed, what they were for, and what should change; the guide is piloted with one resident and one assessor who are not included. Two focus groups (chief residents; administrators) run in the protected half-day. Recordings are transcribed verbatim and de-identified before the programme director sees any transcript. Two analysts code independently at first, then meet to develop themes, keeping a reflexive log.

outcomes.name: Themes on the experience of EPA assessment workload
outcomes.measure: Reflexive thematic analysis of interview and focus-group transcripts, with themes compared across the four roles
outcomes.why: Directly answers how burden is experienced and why assessments are late, brief or strategically chosen.

outcomes.name: Participants' proposals for changing assessment targets
outcomes.measure: Proposals grouped by role, with the reasons participants give
outcomes.timing: Collected in every interview and focus group
outcomes.why: Gives the committee options grounded in participants' reasons, without claiming effects.

outcomes.name: Information power and sample composition
outcomes.measure: Recorded judgement after every fourth interview, with counts by role, training year and assessment count group
outcomes.why: Shows why sampling stopped and who is represented.

outcomes.name: Participant time taken from clinical duties
outcomes.measure: Minutes of clinical time lost per participant, recorded by the research assistant
outcomes.timing: At each interview and focus group
outcomes.why: The study should not add to the burden it examines.

feasibility: The 0.2 FTE research assistant can conduct about two interviews a week alongside transcription; the approved half-days cover both focus groups; no funding is needed beyond existing staff time.
biasMitigation: Interviews by a research assistant without a progression role
De-identified transcripts before the programme director reads them
Purposive invitations to residents with low assessment counts
Two analysts with a reflexive log and a search for negative cases

biasFlags.label: Social desirability and fear of consequences
biasFlags.note: Residents may soften criticism; privacy and the interviewer's independence limit this.

biasFlags.label: Self-selection of vocal participants
biasFlags.note: Those most frustrated may volunteer first; purposive sampling by assessment count balances the sample.

biasFlags.label: Investigator's stake in the current system
biasFlags.note: The programme director does not code transcripts and reads only de-identified material.

flags: App export figures describe the setting only; no quantitative outcome is claimed
parsimony.simplestPath: Interviews and two focus groups in one programme, one thematic analysis, one report to the committee.

theoreticalFramework: None imposed in advance; reflexive thematic analysis with an inductive orientation, using the scoping review's distinction between time, cognitive, emotional and administrative burden only as a sensitising device.
summary: Interviews and focus groups across four roles, one primary thematic outcome, a secondary set of proposals, and process and balancing measures.
